summary: Free __stdcall predicate: for a2 in {1,2,3,4,5} returns whether a1 equals 0; for any other a2 the default path returns false. The switch dispatch reads the jump table at 0x004D9400, and the a1==0 result is computed only for the five accepted mode values. Returns false when a2 is outside the accepted range.

local_names.a1: value tested for equality with zero when a2 is in the accepted range
local_names.a2: mode/selector value; only 1..5 trigger the a1==0 test
local_names.result: bool result, false by default, set to (a1 == 0) for accepted modes

operations.description: Initialize result to false before the switch dispatch.
Switch on a2 via the jump table at 0x004D9400; cases 1 through 5 set result = (a1 == 0), all other values take the default path.
Default case returns false immediately without evaluating a1.
Return result after the switch; true only when a2 was in 1..5 and a1 was zero.
Invoked by sub_4D88D0, whose calling context determines the meaning of the mode values and of the zero test.

unresolved: The semantic meaning of the five accepted a2 values (1..5) and of the a1==0 test depends on the caller sub_4D88D0.
The jump table global 0x004D9400 is a compiler artifact of the switch; its layout is implied by the cases but not directly evidenced here.
